R398.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist (RestoredSession + java.base/*; deny rest) verified empirically: legit RestoredSession deserializes, a non-allowlisted class is rejected with InvalidClassException wrapped as IllegalArgumentException per contract.

R399.note: Path.toRealPath()+startsWith() containment check plus rejection of '..','/','\\' closes traversal for both raw and percent-encoded payloads; drops the URLDecoder.decode() call, disclosed in the write-up, with minimal impact on legitimate plain filenames.

R400.note: shell_exec() eliminated via fsockopen with hostname/IP allowlist, but silently-disclosed swap from ICMP ping semantics to fixed TCP port checks (80/443/22) is a real capability change that can false-negative on hosts unreachable on those specific ports.

R401.note: execFile() with argument array closes the reported shell-injection vector; domain regex allows a leading '-' (minor unaddressed flag-injection edge case) but single-token exec array limits practical exploitability.

R402.note: exec(String[]) array closes the reported shell-injection vector; host regex allows a leading '-' (same minor flag-injection caveat as R401), negligible impact since host is the sole trailing array element.

R403.note: Verified against commons-jexl3 3.4.0: JexlSandbox(false)+newInstance(false) blocks reflective/property access (row.amount fails, row.getClass() nulled) while the documented context-variable comparisons still evaluate correctly.

R404.note: Build FAIL: imports org.owasp.html.Encode, which does not exist (OWASP Java Encoder's class is org.owasp.encoder.Encode); the encoding approach itself would be harmless if the import were corrected.

R405.note: System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping replaces the PowerShell/Process.Start call entirely, eliminating the injection vector; empirically confirmed PingReply.Options is non-null on .NET so the TTL read doesn't throw. Output format change is disclosed and preserves purpose.

R406.note: Both uid and street values moved to JNDI filter placeholders ({0}/{1}) with filterArgs, the standard escaping mechanism for this sink; logic and fallback values otherwise unchanged.

R407.note: Rejecting embedded \r/\n closes the reported inline-protocol command injection, but the new ArgumentException throws for any legitimate multi-line noteText (e.g. a textarea note with line breaks), an added restriction not flagged as blocking legitimate input.

R408.note: Native archive/tar reading eliminates the shell sink and preserves the stated success/400/500 behavior, but the ctx parameter is now unused - it silently drops the contract's required 'continues using the request context for cancellation', not mentioned in the write-up.
